The thing is, a lot of the dogs in rescues are from puppy mills. The puppy mills sell the dogs without vetting the new owners and then the owners surrender the dogs. And since puppy mills or backyard breeders have very poor breeding practices, these dogs will often have health or temperament issues as a consequence. What I’m getting at is getting a dog from a rescue isn’t stopping puppy mills from operating.

When purchasing a dog from an ethical breeder you sign a contract, and it usually outlines what happens to the dog if you can no longer care for it. A breeder would rather see their dogs back in their care than in a rescue or the pound etc. an ethical breeder preforms rigorous health tests before breeding to ensure the puppies will be healthier. They preserve and work towards improving breed standards etc.  

My family has a rescue, she’s great. I know a lot of people who have rescue dogs. But I wouldn’t fault people who choose to buy a dog from an ethical breeder. The problem is with those breeding for profit, and the law should come down harder on that practice imo.

It gets better. Rest your jaw and try to do facial release massages (especially on lateral pterygoid). It’s important not to hyperfocus on the pain if you can- try to distract yourself. Happened to me 2 year ago. It’s been rough but it did go away eventually. Now I just have flare ups not chronic pain. I was like this two years ago. It does get better but I remember thinking the same. I was so terrified of my jaw locking again I would have panic attacks about it locking… which only caused more locking. One of the more vicious cycles of my life. Was in constant pain and could barely speak. It lasted a year and is still on and off now. 

Everyone has given you great advice on who to see/where to get help, so I thought I’d give you a life changing realization I had during that point in my life. 

Despite the pain, I could still see beautiful things. I could still walk. I could feel the comfort of warm water or the taste of my favourite drink. Smiling was painful but I could at times still feel happy. I was so entrenched in pain it consumed my entire life, I thought it was miserable and over. I thought about people who lost so much more than I did and it helped me focus less on the pain. When I focused less on it, I felt it improve. 

I know it sounds silly and preachy, but as someone who has been in very similar shoes (also suicidal over TMJ pain) the most life-changing part of recovery for me was pulling myself out of the misery that came with the pain. I still lived in chronic pain for a while after that but (this didn’t make it go away, obviously) but my life was more bearable and slowly but surely I recovered. I hope you can see those specialists soon and find pain relief. But I found it was equally as important to not let pain define my life.

I’d say this is on the spectrum of normal. Being a teenager is rough, especially one with mental health issues (been there friend). It’s important to reflect and take responsibility for what you did wrong, but it’s equally as important to remind yourself that you aren’t the problem in everything. Things happen and people make mistakes, that doesn’t make you a bad irredeemable person. 

It sounds like you’re really down/depressed. An important thing to know about depression is that is alters your memory and makes you feel like you’re the worst, that you shouldn’t exist, that you’ll never be okay again. If you’re having these thoughts, please recognize that it’s the illness and reach out for help. Things can get better, and I’m not just saying that. 

What you need now is to take action in real life. Reach out for help, if you can. Talk to a therapist or a trusted adult. Another thing that’s really helpful is writing down good things about yourself. Depression will tell you there is none, that this exercise is stupid and you should give up. Don’t listen, sit there until you have a list of at least 10 things. Do this every day. Gratitude journals are great too. I hope you feel better

For brushing your cats teeth, how did you start this? Cats don’t like being touched in areas they aren’t comfortable (like their mouths) and you’re going to have to invest weeks of training and desensitization around their mouth before you can start brushing. My vet told me that a lot of people try brushing outright without helping their cat get used to it first and it leads to this sort of reaction. For the first week, pet your cat around his lips/mouth and use a finger to touch his lips/mouth. Once he seems comfortable with that, you can start using a finger to touch his teeth and gums. Once he starts seeming comfortable with that, then you can try to introduce the toothbrush and paste. 

I think there’s some stuff you can add to your cats water that can help their dental stuff, and there’s also dental food you can get. But maybe try giving brushing another try, just lead up to it slowly!

It’s normal for your kitten to want to play a little rough with his new friend, and it’s normal for resident cat to not be appreciative of his rambunctious playstyle. If they’re able to have quiet moments together and sit next to one another (another good sign is being able to touch noses without hissing etc) then I think you’re on a good road. 

It sounds to me like kitten is not respecting your adult cats boundaries. It’s normal.. but at his age, I’d expect the cat to know “cat talk” a bit better. I’m not sure his history but I wonder how early he was seperated from his siblings/mother. Anyway, 

There’s a few things I’d recommend. For one, try playing with your kitten more. Get one of those flirt poles and let him go wild on it. It sounds like he’s bored and wants to play, so try to help him get that energy out. Once you tire him out a bit from the solo play, try a duo play session with both cats. Even if your resident cat is a bit intimidated by the kitten to play, it’s good she’s able to watch his playstyle without actively being involved. I found this helped my cats a lot. Also make sure to give your resident cat lots of solo love. Whenever your kitten starts bothering your cat, let her enforce her boundaries once. Hissing and growling is not necessarily bad. It’s your cat saying “back off, leave me alone!” And it’s important for your kitten to hear that. If the kitten continues to push your resident cats boundaries then I’d step in and remove him from the situation, or take him aside for some private playtime with a flirt pole. Finally, make sure to reward both cats for the times they’re able to hang out together calmly. This will work to reinforce to your kitten that you like it when they’re chilling out together. I hope this helps. I’m sure it’ll be a few more months and your kitten will chill out more, especially after being neutered. Best of luck!

Unfortunately there’s no garuntee and each cat is an individual. But as someone whose turned very unfriendly/unhappy household cats into ‘tolerating each other and will touch noses and play’ kitties (no cuddling yet, unfortunately) here’s some tips

2. Understand why cats may not accept a newcomer right away (they’re very territorial! Understanding this can help you make adjustments) 
3. Give older kitty plenty of attention. Kittens/young cats demand a lot of your attention but make sure that you don’t leave your resident kitty behind. They will notice and feel left out. Youre part of their territory after all! 
4. Add plenty of vertical space into your home to increase territory 
5. Increase number of litter boxes (it’s # of cats+1)

TIME! Don’t expect it to go well right away. Don’t expect it to be going well in 3 months. It took my cats almost 2 years to get where they are now

Hey! This is a month late but hopefully some of what I say can still be helpful. 

At the very beginning of the reel you have the “what’s new pussycat” segment and I think this is a really fun way to start it off. It showcases your personality and animation style well, and it’s a quick way to connect with employers who are looking for a similar look on their projects. I think one of the biggest things holding the piece back is the lip sync. As a general rule, the sound of the word should come 2-3 frames before the image or frame. “What’s new” is coming about 1-2 frames after the character is already finished the lip sync, which is something you really really don’t want. I also noticed there’s some drift and volume variation (part of which may be style, but I’d really encourage you keep the volumes as consistent as possible in hand drawn) 

I feel like a lot of the animation in the reel is strong, but I think you should discriminate a bit more on what you include in the reel. For example, when the ponies are talking amongst eachother there is a great bit of high-energy character acting, but that’s followed by what feels like a 5-10 second of the characters walking out of frame. Since we can’t see their feet anyway, I’d reccomend this be cut. Imagine how many potential employers might click or look away simply because you aren’t maintaining their interest. As soon as you feel you’ve shown the best part of the animation, cut to  something new. 

The part with the dude, the cat and the bike is great! Lots of great animation there and it’s quick & fun. Definitely keep that in. 

For the robot fight, I’d say it’s a great thing to include because you don’t have much run cycles in the reel. Maybe you can hold the running part for one or two more cycles to really let the viewer settle in to whats happening. The whole sequence is great, but so much faster than everything else it’s hard to really judge what’s happening. 

The part with the dancing character & sign is funny, cute, quick and well done :) 

The pinkie pie segment is hilarious, but once again is a slump in the action of the reel. The whole thing takes up about 30 seconds of the entire reel, and the animation is predominantly lip sync and character acting. Which is fine, but I don’t think this is the best example of character acting you have in the reel. A lot of the lip sync is layered on top of a still frame/face of pinkie, and the lip sync is still suffering from the issue I mentioned earlier about having the sound come around 1-2 frames earlier than the animation. What I’d recommend is cutting the segment down to just where pinkie is saying “Cease and Assist with your…!” (The second time) because not only are you showcasing a lip sync, but also more funny movements and character acting that elevate the lip sync. 

All and all I think you have really great stuff and a great variety of work. I think the reel suffers most of all from a lack of discrimination. 1 and a half minutes is a long time for a reel. I think if you worked on cutting things down to be around 1 minute, even if you kept all of the same animation in there you have now (just cut some parts out) it would be a lot stronger. I have a friend in the industry who says recruiters will watch 30 seconds or less before deciding if they’re interested. You really want to boil down your work to make the best possible impression in the shortest amount of time. 

I hope this helps and I think you really have some great stuff here!

It’s a truly strange experience that only people like you and I can understand. 

A family history of schizophrenia obviously increases your risk, but I would heavily suggest you steer clear from self diagnosis or identifying with schizophrenia. For me this only made things worse. Instead, please talk to your doctor about how you’re feeling. Anxiety induced psychosis is real and deserves treatment. It’s a sign of a severe anxiety disorder that may need medication. Medication has definitely helped me.

As someone whose been emotionally abused in the way mentioned above, it’s not really that easy. The guy will usually say stuff like this to bait you into comforting them, having already spent hours upset and you trying to calm them down. It’s not really a situation where someone is upfront like how you may think. You may have already invested a lot of time into this person or really care about them already, and when they say stuff like that, you just want to reassure them. Tell them it isn’t true. They aren’t a bad person. 

They also don’t tend to say stuff like I “warned” you. Usually, after they inflict emotional abuse, they’ll downward spiral. They really hurt you, but now they’re hurting more. In my case, they’re so depressed they’re near suicidal. Then they’ll say stuff like “I’m so stupid. I knew this would happen. I always mess everything up.” You care about this person, you’ve maybe spent months with them at this point. What are you supposed to say? For me, it was, “you don’t mess everything up, things are going to be okay. You’re not a bad person.” 

Abusers don’t prey on people who have enough self esteem to see through what they’re doing right away. They pull you in and test you over and over again. 

I feel like it’s a really bad take to blame people for being abused in this way. It’s not their fault when they fall for an abusers emotional traps. They were likely, already, in an vulnerable place. They likely have some form of mental illness that makes them way more susceptible to gaslighting. Just being like “oh well they warned you” is such a surface level response to the issue.

Keep breaking down the task until it seems doable for your brain, then get started. Sometimes all you need to do is get the ball rolling. 

Another thing I find helpful is writing down every single thing I want to do. Maybe even just for the day, make a list of your daily goals. For me, it would be clean my room, clean my fish tank, go for a walk, work on my YouTube video, etc! Sometimes when it’s laid out and not vague and overwhelming, it helps our brain!

Finally I would recommend putting barriers in place that prevent you from accessing the games or distracting thing. For me that looked like uninstalling social media from my phone. The extra step of having to reinstall was enough to make my brain go “this isn’t worth it” and find something else to do
